review_scope: Complete Chinese–English alignment read, title and deck included. Complete existing prose retained; eight localized corrections awaiting independent second review.

changes.before: The line appears early in Sunzi's Art of War, and it is probably the single most widely circulated judgment about war in the Chinese language. It is usually taken to mean: fighting is, at bottom, lying.
changes.after: The line appears early in Sunzi's Art of War, and it is one of the most widely circulated judgments about war in the Chinese-speaking world. It is usually taken to mean: fighting is, at bottom, lying.
changes.reason: Restore one of the most, rather than introducing a single top-ranked claim.

changes.before: Scheming is not categorically forbidden here, but it is the mediocre technique. Its long-term structure is less stable than open play, and its legitimacy less clear than strategy's.
changes.after: Scheming is not categorically forbidden here, but it is only a middling technique. Its long-term structure is less stable than open play, and its legitimacy less clear than strategy's.
changes.reason: Retain the source rating 一般 without making it a categorical pejorative; the comparative limitations remain explicit.

changes.before: They know exactly what I intend, where my limits are, what my next move is. And they cannot stop it — because my structural position (resources, time, geography, real capability, standing) makes the move favorable to me, and foreseeing it in full gives them no usable counter.
changes.after: They know exactly what I intend, where my limits are, what my next move is. And they cannot stop it — because my structural position (resources, time, geography, real capability, legitimacy) makes the move favorable to me, and foreseeing it in full gives them no usable counter.
changes.reason: 正当性 is legitimacy; standing risks confusion with subject standing in this framework.

changes.before: The Chinese imperial edict of 127 BCE known as the Order of Extended Grace is the cleanest demonstration. The decree announced that a vassal king's fief would no longer pass intact to his eldest son, but be divided among all his sons.
changes.after: The Chinese imperial edict of 127 BCE known as the Order of Extended Grace is the cleanest demonstration. The decree announced that a vassal king's fief would no longer pass intact to the eldest son of his principal wife, but be divided among all his sons.
changes.reason: Restore 嫡长子 rather than unrestricted eldest son. The underlying historical decree claim remains a separate author question.

changes.before: There is an old line: great deceit resembles sincerity. What it actually points at is exactly this. Push deceit to its limit and it walks out of deceit altogether — because deceit at the limit has to look sincere, and sincerity at the limit becomes transparency. And once you are transparent, the source of your force has to move from the packaging to the structure itself. If the structure holds no advantage, transparency only exposes weakness. If it does, transparency becomes open play.
changes.after: The line "great deceit resembles sincerity" points precisely here. Push deceit to its limit and it walks out of deceit altogether — because deceit at the limit has to look sincere, and sincerity at the limit becomes transparency. And once you are transparent, the source of your force has to move from the packaging to the structure itself. If the structure holds no advantage, transparency only exposes weakness. If it does, transparency becomes open play.
changes.reason: Remove the added historical provenance old; the Chinese only calls it a phrase.

changes.before: This is the crucial step, and it is worth reading twice.
changes.after: This is the crucial step. Please read it slowly.
changes.reason: Preserve the actual request to read slowly, not replace it with reading twice.

changes.before: Third, and most interesting. Its soldiers and citizens notice that the other side does not use deceit, that the other side permits internal questioning, that the other side's operation is transparent. And a thought surfaces: why don't they have to do this? Are we actually the side that is right?
changes.after: Third, and most interesting. Its soldiers and citizens notice that the other side does not use deceit, that the other side permits internal questioning, that the other side's operation is transparent. And a thought surfaces: why don't they do this on their side? Are we actually the side that is right?
changes.reason: Do not add necessity to the observer's question about what the other side does.

changes.before: His hierarchy — attack strategy, then alliances, then troops, and last of all walled cities — means that arms are not all one thing. There are higher and lower positions inside arms. Steering a collision toward strategy is worth more than steering it toward a siege. Drawing that distinction at all is a form of structural self-awareness: it shows Sunzi already felt that "arms" is not a homogeneous toolbox but a field with internal levels.
changes.after: His hierarchy — attack strategy, then alliances, then troops, and last of all walled cities — means that arms are not all one thing. There are higher and lower levels, better and worse techniques, and different structural positions within arms. Steering a collision toward strategy is worth more than steering it toward a siege. Drawing that distinction at all is a form of structural self-awareness: it shows Sunzi already felt that "arms" is not a homogeneous toolbox but a field with internal levels.
changes.reason: Restore all three dimensions listed in the source instead of collapsing them into higher/lower positions.

unresolved_source_questions.finding: Check whether the 127 BCE edict permitted/enabled distribution among children rather than requiring division among all sons; source mandatory wording and universal refusal claim may overstate the primary record. No source amendment made.

metadata_changes.before: Open play draws its force from structural position rather than an information gap, so time is on its side. Deceit's crux is not fooling the enemy but concealing from one's own — and that locks down the entire upward sequence.
metadata_changes.after: Open play draws its force from an asymmetry of structural position rather than an information gap, so time is on its side. Deceit's crux is not fooling the enemy but concealing from one's own — and that locks down the entire upward sequence.
metadata_changes.reason: Restore 结构位势差 rather than structural position alone.
